{{Short description|American theoretical physicist}}
'''Daniel S. Fisher''' (born November 21, 1956) is an American theoretical physicist working in [[statistical physics]].<ref name="stanford profile">{{Cite web|title=Daniel Fisher's Profile {{!}} Stanford Profiles|url=https://profiles.stanford.edu/daniel-fisher|access-date=2021-08-05|website=profiles.stanford.edu|language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Daniel Fisher graduated from [[Cornell University]] with a bachelor's degree in mathematics and physics in 1975 and from [[Harvard University]] with a master's degree in physics in 1978 and a doctorate in physics in 1979 working with [[Bertrand Halperin]].<ref name="math genealogy">{{Cite web|title=Daniel Fisher Math Genealogy|url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=187228|access-date=2021-08-12|website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|language=en}}</ref><ref name="NIH Biosketch">{{Cite web|title=Daniel Fisher NIH Biosketch|url=https://cap.stanford.edu/profiles/viewBiosketch?facultyId=8594&name=Daniel_Fisher|access-date=2021-08-12|website=cap.stanford.edu|language=en}}</ref> He then worked in the theoretical department at [[Bell Labs]] until 1987. In 1987 he became a professor of physics at Princeton University and in 1990 at Harvard.<ref name="NIH Biosketch" /> In 2005 he moved to Stanford University as a professor of applied physics.<ref name="NIH Biosketch" />

Fisher initially focused on dynamics and phase transitions in disordered systems (such as glasses) and quantum dissipation in superconductors. More recently, he switched to [[biophysics]] with a wide range of research topics (including information processing in the brain, physics of biological macromolecules, and evolutionary and population dynamics).<ref name="google scholar">{{Cite web|title=Daniel Fisher Google Scholar|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=WBS6zncAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao|access-date=2021-08-12|website=scholar.google.com|language=en}}</ref>

He has been a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] since 1986.<ref name="APS">{{Cite web|title=Daniel Fisher APS|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1986&unit_id=DCMP&institution=Stanford+University|access-date=2021-08-12|website=www.aps.org|language=en}}</ref> He was a [[Sloan Research Fellow]] from 1988 to 1992. He was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1999 and the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2015. He received the [[Lars Onsager Prize]] in 2013.<ref name="stanford profile" />

He is a son of [[Michael Fisher | Michael E. Fisher]] and brother of [[Matthew P. A. Fisher]].
